Short, honest guidance for household setup, calendar, notifications and account safety.
Set up a verified account and an authoritative household.
Choose a time range, inspect a day and manage real events.
Permission, channels, quiet hours and the honest local test.

Practical steps for passwords, sessions and support.
Important boundaries for this development build.
SharedHouse separates identity verification from household configuration so each server-confirmed step stays clear.
Create an account with an email you can verify and a unique, long password.
Complete email verification before household content becomes available.
Create or edit a household only when the service confirms the change.
If a request fails, review the message and support reference. Do not assume a household change was saved.
The calendar is a household view. It should show actual connected events, not generated examples.
Switch between week, month, quarter and year to change the planning horizon.
Choose a day to open its options and agenda.
Review event details before editing or deleting shared information.
An empty day means no event was returned for that day. It is not a sync-success claim.
SharedHouse uses ordinary Android channels. You decide whether the app may notify and which categories remain enabled.
Read the explanation, then request Android permission only if alerts would help.
Set app categories, quiet hours and a preferred lead time.
Use the local test to verify the Tasks channel without creating server data.
Automatic household reminder evaluation is not connected in this build. No exact alarm is registered.
This build distinguishes service-backed, device-only and unavailable capabilities.
Authentication and household configuration use the authoritative service when connected.
Tutorial, appearance and notification preferences are stored on this device.
Money, task and request activity remain unavailable until their APIs are connected.
Unavailable content is never filled with sample balances, chores, members or sync claims.
Use the smallest amount of information needed to coordinate a household.
Appearance, tutorial and alert choices are device preferences.
Identity and household records are service-backed and role-controlled.
Notification previews use private lock-screen visibility by default.
A complete production Privacy Notice and account-data controls must be connected before release. This screen is a product summary, not that notice.
Account security depends on both the app and careful household use.
Use a unique password of at least 15 characters and never share verification codes.
Treat unexpected session or account alerts as important, but not as emergency messages.
Keep support references when reporting a failed service request; never include your password.
The connected session-storage policy must be reviewed before production. Device-management endpoints are not available in this build.
SharedHouse is household coordination software and does not claim to move money or provide emergency services.
Financial views record household information; they are not a bank account or payment rail.
Notifications are ordinary app messages and must never imitate public emergency alerts.
Production Terms, Privacy Notice and regional notices require approved, versioned content.
This is development guidance, not legal advice or a substitute for approved production terms.
